lessons.name: O aur L — Open/Closed aur Liskov
lessons.desc: Dono tum bana chuke ho. Aaj sirf naam aur naap.
terms: Naye feature ke liye khula, purana code badalne ke liye band.
Bachche ko baap ki jagah rakha ja sake, bina kuch tode.
Wo jagah jahan naya behaviour bina purana code chhoote jud sakta hai.
Bachcha baap se ZYADA specific cheez lauta sakta hai — ye safe hai.
Bachcha baap se ZYADA general cheez maang sakta hai — ye bhi safe hai.
lessons.what:
O — Open/Closed: "Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification." Yaani naya feature jodne ke liye khula, par purana code badalne ke liye band.

Tumne ye Chapter 4 mein bana liya tha. Yaad hai wo git diff --stat jo 0 changes dikha raha tha jab tumne WalletPayment add kiya? Wo Open/Closed ka live proof tha.

L — Liskov Substitution: "Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types." Bachche ko baap ki jagah rakha ja sake, bina kuch tode.

Ye bhi tum kar chuke ho — Chapter 7 mein ElectricCar ne ise toda tha (maxHours 24 se 8), aur tumhara contract test ne use pakda tha.
lessons.why:
Dono ka rishta gehra hai: Liskov toota to Open/Closed apne aap toot jaata hai.

Kyunki agar bachche baap ki jagah nahi chal sakte, to tumhe if (v instanceof ElectricCar) likhna hi padega — aur wahi purana code badalna pad gaya.

Isliye order ye hai: pehle Liskov theek karo (sahi hierarchy ya composition), phir Open/Closed apne aap mil jaata hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Aur ab covariance aur contravariance — jo Liskov ka technical roop hai aur interview mein poochha jaata hai.

Override karte waqt bachcha:

• Return mein baap se zyada specific cheez de sakta hai (covariance) ✓ — kyunki caller ko jo umeed thi wo mil hi raha hai, aur upar se.
• Parameter mein baap se zyada general cheez maang sakta hai (contravariance) ✓ — kyunki jo caller de raha tha wo abhi bhi chalega.

Ulta karoge — return mein kam do, ya parameter mein zyada shart lagao — to Liskov toot jaayega.

Yaad rakhne ka tarika: "lene mein udaar, dene mein sakht." Jitna chaaho lo, par jo waada kiya usse kam mat do.

visual.cap: "Lene mein udaar, dene mein sakht." Bachcha zyada general cheez maang sakta hai aur zyada specific cheez de sakta hai — dono safe. Ulta karne par Liskov tootta hai.

lessons.name: I aur D — Interface Segregation aur Dependency Inversion
lessons.desc: Chhote interfaces, aur upar wale ko neeche par nirbhar mat karo.
terms: Kai chhote interfaces ek bade se behtar hain.
Aisa interface jisme itni methods hon ki koi bhi sab implement nahi kar pata.
Upar wala module neeche wale par nirbhar na ho — dono interface par nirbhar hon.
High = business ka niyam (parking ka logic). Low = tareeka (Postgres, SMS API).
lessons.what:
I — Interface Segregation: "Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use."

Yaani: ek bada interface banane ki jagah kai chhote banao. Warna jo class use implement karegi use aadhi methods khaali chhodni padengi — aur khaali method ek jhooth hai.

D — Dependency Inversion: "High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions."

Tumne ye Chapter 9 mein bana liya tha: ParkingLot ab PostgresSpotRepo par nirbhar nahi, SpotRepository interface par nirbhar hai.
lessons.why:
"Inversion" shabd kyun? Kyunki normally teer upar se neeche jaata hai: ParkingLot → Postgres. Yaani business logic database par nirbhar.

DI ke saath teer ulta ho jaata hai: ParkingLot → SpotRepository ← PostgresSpotRepo. Ab dono interface par nirbhar hain, aur wo interface ParkingLot ke paas rehta hai — business ke paas.

Iska matlab: database ab business logic ka naukar hai, maalik nahi. Database badlo, business logic ek line nahi badlega. Yahi "inversion" hai.

Kaise karna hai:

ISP ke liye ek chhota test: agar koi class kisi interface ki method ko khaali chhod rahi hai ya throw new Error("not supported") likh rahi hai — to interface bahut bada hai.

Aur DIP ke liye: interface kis folder mein rehna chahiye? Jawab jo log galat dete hain: "database wale folder mein". Sahi jawab: business wale folder mein — kyunki wo business ki zarurat hai, database ka offer nahi.

visual.cap: DIP mein teer ulta ho jaata hai. Interface business ke paas rehta hai (uski zarurat hai), aur database use pura karta hai. Isliye database badalne par business logic ek line nahi badalta.

lessons.name: Paanchon ek saath — aur unka rishta
lessons.desc: Ye alag-alag niyam nahi hain. Ek hi cheez ke paanch pehlu hain.
terms: Paanch niyam: SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP.
S aur I — cheezein sahi jagah baithi hain ya nahi.
O, L aur D — cheezein kitni juri hui hain.
lessons.what:
Paanchon ko alag-alag ratna bekaar hai. Wo asal mein do groups mein baithte hain — aur dono groups Chapter 9 wali do cheezein hain:

Cohesion ke niyam (cheezein sahi jagah hain?):
S — ek class, ek badalne ki wajah
I — ek interface, ek tarah ka client

Coupling ke niyam (cheezein kitni juri hain?):
O — naya feature bina purana chhoote jud sake
L — bachcha baap ki jagah chal jaaye
D — business tareeke par nirbhar na ho
lessons.why:
Aur unka aapas mein rishta ye hai:

L toota → O apne aap toot jaata hai (kyunki instanceof likhna padega)
S toota → I aksar toot jaata hai (badi class ka bada interface banta hai)
D toota → test likhna namumkin (asli database chahiye)
I toota → L aksar toot jaata hai (khaali methods waada todti hain)

Isliye ek ko theek karne se aksar doosre apne aap theek ho jaate hain — jaisa tumne dekha: Chapter 8 mein composition lagane se L aur O dono theek ho gaye the.

Kaise karna hai:

Interview ke liye ek line ka jawab har niyam ke liye — aur saath mein apne code se ek example. Wahi tumhe baaki sabse alag karega:

S — "Ek class, ek badalne ki wajah. Maine ParkingLot se pricing aur notification alag kiye, kyunki unhe finance aur marketing badalwaate the."
O — "Naye ke liye khula, purane ke liye band. Maine PaymentMethod interface banaya; naya wallet payment jodne par ParkingLot mein 0 lines badle."
L — "Bachcha baap ki jagah chale. Mera ElectricCar extends Car isko tod raha tha, to maine use composition mein badla."
I — "Chhote interfaces. Meri Bike ko charge() khaali chhodni pad rahi thi, to maine Chargeable alag kiya."
D — "Business tareeke par nirbhar na ho. ParkingLot SpotRepository par nirbhar hai, PostgresSpotRepo par nahi."
gotchas: SOLID ko checklist ki tarah andha mat chalao. Ye niyam hain, kanoon nahi. Har ek ki apni keemat hai (zyada files, zyada interfaces) aur choti scripts mein wo keemat faayde se zyada ho sakti hai.
Interview mein sirf definition mat batao. Har niyam ke saath apne code ka ek example do — "maine ye toota dekha aur aise theek kiya". Wahi asli jawab hai.
Paanchon ko 100% follow karne ki koshish mein code 3 guna bada ho jaata hai. Sochо: is jagah ye niyam kaunsi asli problem se bacha raha hai?

units.title: Patterns — jinhe tumne pehle hi bana liya

lessons.name: Strategy aur Factory — tum ye bana chuke ho
lessons.desc: Behaviour ko object banao. Aur object banane ko naam do.
terms: Ek jaani-mani problem ka jaana-maana hal, jise ek naam mila hua ho.
Behaviour ko ek object bana kar bahar se dena — taaki wo badla ja sake.
Object banane ka kaam ek alag jagah rakhna, taaki caller ko "kaun sa" ka faisla na karna pade.
Ek static method jo sahi object bana kar deti hai. Sabse aam roop.
lessons.what:
Strategy pattern: "Ek kaam karne ke kai tarike hain. Har tarike ko ek object bana do, aur jo chahiye wo bahar se de do."

Tumne ye teen baar banaya:

• PaymentMethod — paisa lene ke kai tarike (Ch 4)
• PowerSource, ServiceLevel — gaadi ki khoobiyan (Ch 8)
• PricingPolicy — fee nikalne ke kai tarike (Ch 10)

Factory pattern: "Object banane ka faisla ek jagah rakho, taaki caller ko na sochna pade ki kaunsa banana hai."

Ye bhi tumne Chapter 2 mein bana liya tha: Lot.withFloors("Airport", 5, 100).
lessons.why:
Ab dekho ki naam kyu zaroori hai. Ek team meeting mein do baatein:

Bina naam ke: "Main soch raha hu ki pricing ke logic ko ek interface ke peeche daal dein aur constructor se pass karein taaki weekend wali alag ho sake aur test mein nakli de sakein..."

Naam ke saath: "Pricing ko Strategy bana dete hain."

Bas. Yahi patterns ka asli faayda hai — baat karne ki bhasha. Wo naya design nahi dete; wo tumhare bane hue design ko ek naam dete hain.

Kaise karna hai:

Ek chetavani jo bahut zaroori hai: pattern pehle mat chuno.

Galat tarika: "chalo yahan Factory pattern lagate hain."
Sahi tarika: "yahan ye problem hai... (hal nikalta hai)... arre, iska naam Factory hai."

Pattern pehle chunne se over-engineering hoti hai — jaise ek chhote script mein 4 interfaces aur ek AbstractFactory. Wo kisi problem ka hal nahi hota, wo sirf pattern ka pradarshan hota hai.

Factory ke andar ka switch theek hai — wo ek hi jagah hai jahan bahar ka data objects mein badalta hai. Us switch ko har jagah copy karna galat hai.
Strategy ke liye 4 interfaces bana kar ek chhoti script ko 300 line ka mat bana do. Strategy tab chahiye jab behaviour sach mein badalta ho.

lessons.name: Observer aur Decorator — do naye
lessons.desc: Ek batata hai "kuch hua", doosra cheez ke upar cheez chadhata hai.
terms: Ek cheez badle to jinhe matlab hai unhe khud-ba-khud khabar mil jaaye.
Wo cheez jispe kuch hota hai.
Ek object ke upar ek aur object chadha kar naya behaviour jodna, bina purana badle.
lessons.what:
Observer: "Jab kuch hota hai, to jinhe matlab hai unhe khabar mil jaaye — aur jisko kuch hua use ye pata na ho ki kaun sun raha hai."

Hamare parking lot mein: gaadi park hui to display board update ho, analytics record kare, aur SMS jaaye. ParkingLot ko in teeno ka pata nahi hona chahiye.

Decorator: "Ek object ko dusre object mein lapet do, taaki naya behaviour jud jaaye — bina purana object badle."

Parking mein: base pricing ke upar weekend surge, uske upar loyalty discount, uske upar GST. Har ek ek layer.
lessons.why:
Observer ka faayda: ParkingLot ka code kabhi nahi badalta chahe 10 naye listeners aa jaayein. Ye Open/Closed ka seedha roop hai.

Aur tum ise pehchante ho — addEventListener bilkul yahi hai. Button ko nahi pata ki uspe kaun sun raha hai.

Decorator ka faayda: layers ko kisi bhi kram mein aur kitni bhi jodi ja sakti hain. Inheritance se ye karna Chapter 7 wala explosion bana deta (SurgeGstPricing, LoyaltySurgeGstPricing...).

Kaise karna hai:

Decorator ki pehchaan: wo ussi interface ko implement karta hai jise wo lapet raha hai. Isliye bahar wale ko farak hi nahi padta ki wahan ek layer hai ya paanch.

Ek chhoti chetavani Observer ke liye: agar koi listener error phenk de to baaki listeners chhoot jaayenge. Har listener ko try/catch mein lapeto.

lessons.name: Template Method, aur Singleton ka sach
lessons.desc: Ek dhaancha jisme khaali jagah bhari jaati hai. Aur ek pattern jise aksar hata dena chahiye.
terms: Baap kaam ka dhaancha likhta hai, bachche khaali jagah bharte hain.
Wo khaali jagah jise bachcha bhar sakta hai.
Aisa pattern jisme class ka sirf ek hi object ban sakta hai.
Aisi cheez jo poore program mein ek hi ho aur kahin se bhi chhui ja sake.
lessons.what:
Template Method: baap poore kaam ka kram likh deta hai, aur kuch kadam abstract chhod deta hai jo bachche bharte hain.

Parking mein: "gaadi andar aane ka tarika" hamesha ek hi hai — validate, spot dhundo, allot, ticket banao, khabar do. Par har lot mein spot dhundhne ka tarika alag ho sakta hai.

Singleton: "is class ka sirf ek object ban sakta hai, aur wo poore program mein ek hi jagah se milta hai."
lessons.why:
Ab Singleton ke baare mein sach, kyunki ye interview mein poochha jaata hai aur zyadatar log sirf uska code bata dete hain:

Singleton asal mein global variable hai, ek class ke mukhaute mein. Aur uske teen bade nuksaan hain:

1. Test namumkin ho jaata hai — ek test ki state agle test mein reh jaati hai. Test order matter karne lagta hai.
2. Chhupi hui nirbharta — Config.getInstance() class ke andar likha hota hai, constructor mein nahi dikhta. Padhne wale ko pata hi nahi chalta ki ye class Config par nirbhar hai.
3. DIP tootta hai — tum concrete class par nirbhar ho jaate ho, interface par nahi.

Kaise karna hai:

Zyadatar cases mein Singleton ka sahi ilaaj DI hai (Chapter 9): ek hi object banao — main.ts mein — aur jise chahiye use pass kar do.

Tumhe "ek hi object" ka faayda mil jaata hai, aur teeno nuksaan gayab ho jaate hain: test mein alag object de sakte ho, nirbharta constructor mein dikhti hai, aur tum interface par nirbhar rehte ho.

Interview ka best jawab: "Singleton ek object ki ginti control karta hai, par usse global state ban jaata hai aur testability chali jaati hai. Main aksar ek instance banata hu aur use inject kar deta hu — faayda wahi, nuksaan zero."
gotchas: Template method (park()) ko final/override-proof rakhna chahiye — agar bachcha use override kar de to poora kram tehas-nehas ho jaayega. TypeScript mein final nahi hai, to comment se batao.
Bahut saare hooks dena Template Method ko samajhne layak nahi chhodta. 2-3 se zyada hooks ho to Strategy behtar hai.
Singleton ko "thread safety" ke sawaal se mat jodo — JavaScript single threaded hai. Asli sawaal testability aur chhupi hui nirbharta ka hai.
Kuch cheezein sach mein ek honi chahiye (database connection pool, logger). Par tab bhi ek instance banao aur inject karo — getInstance() mat likho.

lessons.name: Builder aur Adapter — do jo roz kaam aate hain
lessons.desc: Ek lambe constructor ka ilaaj hai, doosra purane code ko apne code se jodne ka.
terms: Ek object ko kadam-dar-kadam banane ka tarika, jahan har kadam ka naam ho.
Aisi methods jo khud ko wapas karti hain, taaki chain likhi ja sake.
Ek cheez ko dusre interface mein lapetna, taaki wo tumhare code ke saath chal sake.
Bahar ka code jo tumne nahi likha aur jise tum badal nahi sakte.
lessons.what:
Do patterns jo machine coding interview aur asli kaam — dono mein sabse zyada aate hain.

Builder: jab object banane ke liye 6-7 cheezein chahiye, jinme se kuch optional hon. Constructor mein new ParkingLot("A", 5, 100, 0, true, null, 30) likhna ek paheli ban jaata hai.

Adapter: jab bahar ka code (koi library, purana SDK) tumhare interface se match nahi karta. Tum use badal nahi sakte, to use lapet lo.
lessons.why:
Builder ki asli wajah sirf "padhne mein achha" nahi hai. Do gehri wajah hain:

1. Object banne tak adhoora rehta hai, aur build() par ek baar mein validate hota hai. Yaani "aadha bana object" (Chapter 2) kabhi bahar nahi jaata.
2. Optional cheezein ke liye 6 alag constructors nahi banane padte (aur TypeScript mein overloading asli hai bhi nahi — Chapter 6).

Adapter ki wajah DIP hai (Chapter 10). Tumhara domain PaymentMethod maangta hai. Bahar ki library RazorpayClient deti hai jiska interface bilkul alag hai. Adapter beech mein khada hokar dono ko jodta hai — aur tumhara domain us library ka naam bhi nahi jaanta.

Kaise karna hai:

Builder ka ek zaroori niyam: validation build() mein karo, har setter mein nahi. Kyunki beech ke kadamon mein object ka adhoora hona theek hai — wo abhi ban raha hai. Asli check tab hona chahiye jab wo bahar jaa raha ho.

Aur Adapter ka: adapter ko infra/ mein rakho, domain/ mein nahi. Kyunki wo bahar ki duniya ko jaanta hai — aur domain ko bahar ki duniya ka pata nahi hona chahiye (Chapter 10 ka DIP).

Ek chhota bonus: Adapter test ko bahut aasan bana deta hai. Asli Razorpay ki jagah ek FakePayment do — kaam ho gaya, bina kisi network call ke.

visual.cap: Builder: adhoora object andar rehta hai, build() par ek baar validate hokar bahar aata hai. Adapter: bahar ki library ko lapet kar apne interface mein badal do — domain ko uska naam bhi pata nahi chalta.

units.title: Anti-patterns — testing, aur OOP ki seema

lessons.name: Anti-patterns — jinke naam pad gaye
lessons.desc: God object, anemic model, aur wo galtiyan jo tumne khud ki thin.
terms: Aisa hal jo pehle theek lagta hai par baad mein problem ban jaata hai.
Ek class jo sab kuch jaanti hai aur sab kuch karti hai.
Aisi classes jinme sirf data ho aur koi behaviour na ho — procedural code classes ke mukhaute mein.
Ek method jo apni class se zyada doosri class ka data use karti ho.
Har cheez ko number/string rakhna, jabki uske apne niyam hain.
lessons.what:
Anti-pattern matlab aisa hal jo pehle theek lagta hai aur baad mein bojh ban jaata hai. Paanch sabse aam:

1. God object — ek class jo sab kuch karti hai. Tumhari Chapter 9 wali ParkingLot is raaste par thi: park, unpark, fee, SMS, report, CSV.

2. Anemic domain model — classes mein sirf data, saara logic alag "Service" classes mein. Ye SRP ko bahut door le jaane se hota hai.

3. Feature envy — ek method jo apne data se zyada doosre ke data se khelti hai.

4. Primitive obsession — Chapter 9 wali Money se pehle wala haal.

5. Shotgun surgery — ek chhota badlav, paanch file (Chapter 6 wala if-else).
lessons.why:
Anemic domain model par thoda rukо, kyunki ye sabse chhupa hua hai.

Bahut se codebases mein aisa dikhta hai: class Ticket { id; plate; enteredAt; } — sirf data. Aur phir class TicketService { calculateHours(t); isExpired(t); } — saara logic.

Ye chalti hai. Par ye procedural code hi hai, bas classes ka mukhauta laga kar. Data ek jagah, uspe kaam karne wale functions doosri jagah — bilkul Chapter 1 wali problem, aur wahi nuksaan: koi bhi Service Ticket ka data badal sakti hai.

Aur ek imaandar baat: bade systems mein ye kabhi-kabhi jaan-boojh kar chuna jaata hai (jab data DB se aata ho aur logic alag layers mein ho). To ise andha "bura" mat kehna — bas jaan lo ki tum kya chun rahe ho.

Kaise karna hai:

God object pehchanne ke teen naap:

1. File 300+ line ki hai
2. Class 10+ public methods rakhti hai
3. Ek line ka kaam bina 2+ "aur" ke nahi likha ja sakta

Aur feature envy ka test: agar ek method this se zyada kisi aur object ko chhoo rahi hai, to wo method galat class mein hai. Use uthake wahan le jao jahan uska data hai.

lessons.name: Testing — design ka aaina
lessons.desc: Jo test karna mushkil hai, wo design bhi bura hai. Hamesha.
terms: Ek chhoti cheez ka akela test, bina database/network ke.
Asli cheez ki jagah rakha gaya nakli object.
Nakli cheez jo bas ek tay kiya hua jawab deti hai.
Nakli cheez jo ye bhi yaad rakhti hai ki use kaise bulaya gaya.
Nakli cheez jisme sach mein chhota sa kaam karne wala code hota hai.
Har method ke teen waade: kya chahiye (pre), kya milega (post), aur kya hamesha sach rahega (invariant).
lessons.what:
Testing ka sabse bada faayda bug pakadna nahi hai. Wo hai: testing tumhara design tumhe wapas dikha deti hai.

Agar test likhna mushkil hai, to wajah hamesha in mein se ek hoti hai:

• Class apni cheezein khud banati hai → DIP toota (Ch 9)
• Class bahut kuch karti hai → SRP toota (Ch 10)
• Bahut kuch setup karna padta hai → coupling zyada
• Test order matter karta hai → global state / Singleton (Ch 11)

Yaani test likhne mein dard = design mein bimari. Test ko theek karne ki jagah design theek karo.
lessons.why:
Aur teen tarah ke nakli objects hote hain, jinke naam interview mein poochhe jaate hain:

Stub — bas ek tay jawab deta hai. FakeClock jo hamesha ek hi time de.
Mock — ye bhi yaad rakhta hai ki kaise bulaya gaya. FakeNotifier jo sent[] array rakhta hai.
Fake — asli kaam ka chhota version. ArraySpotRepo asli PostgresSpotRepo ki jagah.

Practically: Fake sabse achha hota hai, kyunki wo sach mein kaam karta hai. Mock ka zyada istemaal test ko implementation se bandh deta hai — refactor karo to test toot jaate hain, chahe behaviour same ho.

Kaise karna hai:

Aur ek cheez jo OOP mein khaas hai: Design by Contract. Har public method ke teen waade hote hain:

Precondition — "mujhe kya chahiye" (plate khaali na ho)
Postcondition — "main kya doonga" (ticket ya null, aur spot bhar jaayegi)
Invariant — "kya hamesha sach rahega" (earnings kabhi negative nahi)

lessons.name: OOP vs FP — aur OOP kab galat hai
lessons.desc: Do soch, do tarah ke faayde. Aur imaandari se: OOP har jagah sahi nahi hai.
terms: Aisi soch jahan data aur function alag rehte hain, aur data badalta nahi (immutable).
Wahi input do to wahi output, aur duniya mein kuch na badle.
Ek chunav: naye TYPES jodna aasan chahiye ya naye OPERATIONS jodna.
lessons.what:
OOP aur FP ko log "dushman" ki tarah dekhte hain. Wo galat hai — dono ek hi problem ke do jawab hain, aur dono ka apna faayda hai.

OOP: data aur uspe kaam karne wale functions ek saath, aur data chhupa hua.
FP: data saada aur khula, functions alag, aur data kabhi badalta nahi — badalna ho to naya banta hai.

Aur mazedaar baat: tumne is kitaab mein dono use kiye. Money aur PlateNumber immutable value objects hain — wo FP ki soch hai, OOP ke andar.
lessons.why:
Asli farak ek chunav mein hai jise expression problem kehte hain:

OOP mein naya type jodna aasan hai (nayi class banao, koi purana code nahi badla) par naya operation jodna mushkil (har class mein method add karni padegi).

FP mein ulta: naya operation jodna aasan (naya function likho) par naya type jodna mushkil (har function ka switch badalna padega).

Isliye sawaal ye hai: tumhare system mein kya zyada badalta hai — types ya operations?

Parking lot mein types zyada badalte hain (naye vehicle, naye payment method) — isliye OOP sahi choice hai. Ek data-processing pipeline mein operations zyada badalte hain — wahan FP behtar hai.

Kaise karna hai:

Aur ab imaandari se — OOP kab galat choice hai:

1. Chhoti scripts. 50 line ka data script — usme 4 interfaces aur DI daalna over-engineering hai.
2. Data transformation. Ek CSV padho, filter karo, sum karo — wahan map/filter/reduce classes se kahin behtar hai.
3. Jab koi state hi na ho. Ek pure calculation — usko class mein lapetna bekaar hai.
4. Bahut zyada concurrency. Shared mutable state race conditions banata hai. Wahan immutable data safe hai.

Best jawab aksar mila-jula hota hai: bahar OOP (structure, boundaries), andar FP (calculations, transformations). Jaisa tumne kiya — OOP classes jinke andar immutable Money aur pure calculate() methods.

Chhoti scripts mein interfaces aur DI daalna over-engineering hai. Sochо: "ye code 6 mahine mein badlega ya ek baar chal kar khatam ho jaayega?"

lessons.name: Architecture review — peeche mud kar dekho
lessons.desc: Kya banaya, kya chhoda, aur har faisle ki keemat kya thi.
terms: Apne hi design ko bahar se dekhna aur uske faisle likhna.
Har faisle ki keemat — jo mila uske badle jo chhoda.
Code ka ek hissa jiski apni zimmedari ho aur jo sirf apne neeche wale ko jaanta ho.
lessons.what:
Poori kitaab ka safar ek line mein: ek 60-line procedural file se ek layered, tested, extensible system tak.

Aur us safar ke har mod par ek faisla tha. Review ka matlab hai un faislon ko likhna — aur unki keemat bhi.

Kyunki har achhe design ki ek keemat hoti hai. Composition ne classes 24 se 4 ki, par objects ki ginti badha di. DI ne test 3 line ke kar diye, par ek composition root ki zarurat pada di.
lessons.why:
Junior aur senior mein farak yahi hota hai:

Junior batata hai: "maine ye banaya."
Senior batata hai: "maine ye chuna, ye chhoda, aur ye tab galat ho jaayega."

Aur interview mein sabse strong jawab wahi hota hai. "Encapsulation kya hai" ka jawab har koi de deta hai. "Maine apne parking lot mein encapsulation isliye lagaya kyunki maine khud 4 attacks likh kar dekhe the, aur uske baad wo 4 attacks compile hi nahi hote the" — ye jawab koi aur nahi de sakta.

Kaise karna hai:

Review mein chaar hisse hone chahiye:

1. Layers — kaunsi layer kya jaanti hai, aur kya nahi jaanti.
2. Faisle — kya socha, kya chuna, kya chhoda, kyu.
3. Naap — har chapter ke before/after numbers ek jagah.
4. Seemayein — kya abhi bhi kharab hai, aur agar system 10 guna bada ho to kya pehle tootega.

Chautha hissa sabse zyada impress karta hai, kyunki wo dikhata hai ki tum apne kaam se pyaar nahi, uska hisaab rakhte ho.

Ek parking lot system, TypeScript mein, zero dependencies.

lessons.name: Elevator System — ab akele karo
lessons.desc: Naya domain, koi hint nahi. Sirf requirements aur ek checklist.
terms: Ek jagah seekhi hui cheez ko dusri jagah lagana — asli seekhne ka yahi paimana hai.
Kya banana hai, bina ye bataye ki kaise.
Kisi cheez ki abhi ki haalat — jaise lift "ruki hui hai" ya "upar ja rahi hai".

Aisi cheez jiski gini-chuni haalatein hoti hain, aur wo sirf tay kiye hue raaston se ek haalat se doosri mein jaati hai. Jaise lift: ruki → upar ja rahi → darwaza khula → ruki. Lift "upar ja rahi" se seedha "darwaza khula" nahi ho sakti — pehle rukna padega.
lessons.what:
Ab ek naya system. Aur is baar koi step-by-step nahi.

Requirements:

• Ek building mein kai lifts hain, aur kai floors
• Log kisi bhi floor se lift bula sakte hain (upar ya neeche ke liye)
• Lift ke andar log floor button dabate hain
• System ko tay karna hai ki kaunsi lift kaunsi request lega
• Lift ki apni haalat hoti hai: chal rahi hai (upar/neeche), ruki hui, darwaza khula
• Kuch lifts service mode mein ho sakti hain (koi request nahi lengi)
• Kuch lifts sirf kuch floors par rukti hain (jaise sirf even floors)
• Emergency mein sab lifts ground floor par jaayein aur darwaza khol dein
lessons.why:
Ye jaan-boojh kar parking lot se alag hai:

Parking lot mein cheezein rukti hain (spot bhari ya khali). Elevator mein cheezein chalti hain — lift ki haalat har second badalti hai.

Yaani yahan ek nayi cheez aayegi jo parking mein nahi thi: state machine. Aur us par bhi wahi sawaal lagenge jo tumne poori kitaab mein seekhe.

Kaise karna hai:

Kaam karne ka tarika — bilkul wahi jo is kitaab mein tha:

1. Pehle procedural likho. Ganda, ek file. Aur usko todo.
2. Classes nikalo. Har ek ka kaam ek line mein likho.
3. Kya badal sakta hai? Wo interface banega. (Kaunsi lift chunni hai — ye strategy hai.)
4. Kya ek jaisi cheez ke kai roop hain? Wo polymorphism hai. (Normal lift, service lift, even-floor lift.)
5. Kya inject karna hai? (Clock — kyunki lift ke movement ka test bina asli waqt ke hona chahiye.)
6. Har contract likho, phir test likho.

Aur ek hint jo main de raha hu kyunki wo naya hai: lift ki haalat ke liye if-else ka pahaad mat banao. Sochо ki haalat khud ek cheez ho sakti hai.
